Hypothesis: TBC1D2B restrains E-cadherin internalisation in epithelial cells, so its loss could reduce surface E-cadherin in gingival epithelium. The E-cadherin result comes from lung cancer cells overexpressing TBC1D2B, and gingival E-cadherin has been examined in one patient only.
The jaw lesions occur only with biallelic loss of TBC1D2B, but no study has examined how. The proposed route through RAB5, RAC1 and NF-kB/NFATc1 signalling in osteoclast progenitors is a hypothesis.

nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift and splice alleles abolish or sharply reduce TBC1D2B mRNA and protein in patient cells; in the one compound heterozygote with a missense allele, protein is halved. TBC1D2B is a TBC-domain RAB GTPase-activating protein, so its loss removes a RAB GAP activity, whose best-characterised substrate is RAB7.
